title: Tourism is moving from rebound to managed growth as geopolitical, climate, infrastructure, digital, and community pressures converge
geography: 53 OECD and partner countries; tourism performance, policy, resilience, social benefits, and extreme-weather adaptation

denominator.unit: OECD and partner countries covered by the report

international_arrivals_2024.unit: international tourist arrivals to OECD countries in 2024

arrival_change_2024.unit: percent increase in OECD international tourist arrivals in 2024

arrival_change_2025.unit: estimated percent increase in arrivals during 2025

economic_significance.value: Tourism directly contributed 4.0% of GDP and 19.3% of services exports in OECD countries

observations.method: OECD synthesis of tourism statistics, policy developments, country profiles, and thematic analysis across 53 OECD and partner countries.
observations.uncertainty: Arrival, GDP, and services-export measures are aggregate country-level indicators; they do not show local retention, job quality, resident welfare, seasonality, or distribution across firms and communities.
observations.subgroup: Visitors, tourism workers, destination residents, firms, transport and hospitality providers, governments, and communities dependent on visitor spending.
observations.counterinterpretation: Strong tourism demand can support jobs, exports, local enterprise, and cultural exchange, while some destinations may deliberately limit volume or prioritize non-tourism development.

risk_convergence.value: Geopolitical tensions, conflict, safety concerns, affordability, and extreme weather are jointly shaping near-term travel patterns and operating risk

management_shift.value: Policy priorities are shifting from restoring demand toward managing visitor flows, crisis preparedness, resilience, and balanced economic, social, and environmental outcomes

coordination_route.value: Whole-of-government and multi-level coordination is increasingly treated as necessary for tourism governance

observations.method: OECD executive-summary synthesis of tourism policy reforms, country practices, geopolitical risk, and extreme-weather adaptation priorities.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies policy direction and risk channels rather than estimating a universal causal effect of any single shock on travel, prices, or community outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Destinations, local authorities, tourism businesses, transport systems, residents, visitors, and emergency or climate-risk managers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Flexible coordination may improve resilience, but it can also increase administrative burdens or centralize decisions unless local communities have meaningful authority.

observations.period: 2026; social benefits and local value creation

denominator.unit: tourism destinations and communities discussed in OECD policy analysis

concentration_pressure.value: Concentrated visitor flows pressure infrastructure and communities while less-visited places miss potential tourism benefits

community_route.value: The report recommends empowering local communities, spreading flows to prepared areas, investing in shared infrastructure, supporting local businesses, and integrating tourism with regional development

value_model.value: Tourism success is increasingly framed as sustained local economic value plus resilience, environmental stewardship, and positive community outcomes

observations.method: OECD thematic analysis of social benefits, destination governance, local value creation, visitor management, and regional development practices.
observations.uncertainty: Policy recommendations do not establish that local value creation or flow-spreading has occurred uniformly or that any particular intervention resolves crowding, displacement, or inequality.
observations.subgroup: Host communities, local businesses, residents, destination authorities, cultural assets, rural and less-visited regions, and visitors.
observations.counterinterpretation: Visitor concentration can be efficient for infrastructure and revenue, and tourism growth may generate resources for preservation; distributional effects vary by place, ownership, and governance.

observations.period: 2026; digitalisation, AI, infrastructure, and extreme-weather adaptation

digital_route.value: Digitalisation and AI are presented as tools for destination management, operational efficiency, personalised experiences, and more timely tourism data

adaptation_route.value: Tourism planning increasingly requires risk assessment, early warning, crisis response, resilient infrastructure, nature-based solutions, and adaptation skills

enabling_conditions.value: Skills, finance, streamlined regulation, reliable transport, connectivity, and support for SMEs are identified as conditions for a competitive and resilient transition

observations.method: OECD synthesis of digital transformation, AI, infrastructure, skills, finance, climate adaptation, and tourism-business policy evidence.
observations.uncertainty: The publication does not measure AI effectiveness, data quality, algorithmic distributional effects, infrastructure performance, or the frequency and severity of local weather losses in a common causal design.
observations.subgroup: Tourism SMEs, workers, digital providers, destination managers, transport operators, residents, visitors, and communities exposed to extreme weather.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital tools and resilient infrastructure can improve access and safety, but can also increase surveillance, vendor dependence, exclusion, or energy and maintenance costs.

related_sources.claim: Complementary cross-economy index evidence on tourism capability, cultural resources, openness, affordability, and workforce constraints.
Complementary migration and mobility context for cross-border movement and geopolitical mobility conditions.

boundary: This record adds an official OECD policy and sector-performance lens on tourism as a coupled cultural, consumer, infrastructure, climate, labor, digital, and geopolitical system. It uses aggregate indicators and policy synthesis, not respondent-level data, individual travel histories, household affordability, worker wages, resident sentiment, causal tourism effects, or proof that recommendations were implemented.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official OECD publication page and executive summary reviewed for coverage, arrivals, economic contribution, geopolitical and weather risk, visitor concentration, community benefits, digitalisation, AI, infrastructure, skills, and adaptation priorities.
